definition: Fake nude photography is the creation of nude photographs designed to appear as genuine nudes of an individual.
details: The motivations for the creation of these modified photographs include curiosity, sexual gratification, the stigmatization or embarrassment of the subject, and commercial gain, such as through the sale of the photographs via pornographic websites. Fakes can be created using image editing software or through generative artificial intelligence. Fake images created using the latter method are called deepfakes, including deepfake pornography.

explainer.lead: Fake nude photography turns ordinary pictures or composites into images meant to look like real nude photographs of a particular person. It can be done with ordinary editing software or generative AI, and it matters because the fakes can humiliate targets, enable extortion, and be sold or spread online.

tiers.eli5: Imagine cutting someone's face from a school photo and gluing it onto a drawing of an unclothed body so the picture looks real. Computers can make that kind of trick much more convincing, or invent a fake body from a clothed photo. Even though the picture is false, it can seriously hurt and embarrass the person shown.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers are most likely to encounter this problem in trust-and-safety, image-forensics, or generative-image systems. Relevant methods range from conventional compositing to GANs and newer generative models, delivered through downloadable tools, messaging bots, or paid websites. Pitfalls include treating AI-generated imagery as the only route to a fake, assuming withdrawal removes copied software, and overlooking biased outputs such as DeepNude's female-only results.
tiers.paperLevel: Let P be a real person and X a set of source images. A fake nude is an image Y synthesized or edited so that viewers are intended to interpret Y as an authentic nude photograph of P; common operators are face/body compositing and clothing removal, implemented with image editors or neural networks. Deepfakes are the generative-AI subset, and reported limitations include DeepNude's gender-biased output from imbalanced training data and the persistence of copied software after withdrawal.

explainer.example: DeepNude, released in June 2019, used a generative adversarial network to turn images of women into nude-looking pictures. Because its creator had more nude images of women than men, it produced female bodies even when the original subject was male; the application was withdrawn on June 27, but copies continued to circulate.

usedIn.name: DeepNude
usedIn.detail: A Windows and Linux application released in June 2019 that used a generative adversarial network to produce nude-looking images from pictures of women.

usedIn.name: Deepfake Telegram bot
usedIn.detail: A free service launched in July 2019 that accepted submitted photos and returned manipulated nude images within minutes.

usedIn.name: Dreamtime
usedIn.detail: A free successor application to DeepNude, copies of which remained available after its release.

usedIn.name: Nudify websites
usedIn.detail: By late 2024, most services for turning clothed photographs into nude images were websites rather than apps and required payment.

explainer.intuition: The image borrows a real person's identity while inventing or borrowing the nude body shown. Its persuasive power comes from presenting that fabrication as an authentic photograph rather than an obvious illustration.
howItWorks: A creator starts with imagery associated with the target, often a clothed photograph.
One route superimposes the target's face onto an existing nude image.
Another route uses editing software or a neural network to make a clothed source image appear unclothed.
The resulting image is presented as genuine and may be posted, sold, or circulated online.
explainer.whyItMatters: Targets can suffer psychological harm, public discrediting, embarrassment, and extortion, and the images can also be distributed for commercial gain. Performers, politicians, and businesspeople have been prominent targets, while disputed images can lead to legal threats and public controversy.
misconceptions: Not every fake nude is a deepfake: older fakes can be made entirely with conventional image-editing software.
A clothing-removal tool does not reveal someone's real body; it generates an invented nude appearance.
A nude-looking output is not necessarily pornographic, as illustrated by the typically non-pornographic images produced by DeepNude.
